title: A low-income community-solar connector creates a bill-credit route without proving household savings
source_unit: U.S. Department of Energy and HHS Clean Energy Connector program page; low-income community-solar implementation design and pilot route, not a household outcome sample
geography: United States; initial pilot in Washington, D.C., Illinois, New Mexico, Massachusetts, Maryland, and Rhode Island

observations.period: March 2024-2026 page status; pilot launch and six-jurisdiction expansion

eligibility_route.value: LIHEAP recipients can be identified for access to community-solar subscriptions with savings

household_choice.value: eligible households opt in and subscription managers complete enrollment

minimum_bill_credit_discount.unit: percent minimum difference between household financial benefit and participation cost

consumer_protection.value: the program describes consumer protections, clear communication, disclosures, and data safeguards across enrollment and participation

household_enrollment_and_bill_effect.value: not observed in the public page
household_enrollment_and_bill_effect.unit: missing household enrollment, opt-in completion, bill credit, subscription fee, payment timing, persistence, energy burden, or exit outcome

observations.method: DOE official Clean Energy Connector page review; eligibility, opt-in, subscription-manager handoff, minimum savings rule, pilot jurisdictions, and protections are coded separately from household-level participation and bill outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The page describes a program route and requirements, not the number of eligible households, completed enrollments, realized credits, net savings, retention, or household energy-security change.
observations.subgroup: LIHEAP-eligible and participating low-income households; access may vary by state program, utility territory, language, digital access, housing tenure, and subscription availability.
observations.counterinterpretation: A required minimum discount and opt-in route can improve the terms of community-solar participation, but households may still face outreach, eligibility verification, separate billing, housing, or provider-availability barriers.

related_sources.claim: DOE describes utility bill credits and low-income community-solar treatment for assisted households.
DOE's annual update describes the Connector's household identification and subscription-manager handoff concept.

boundary: This record adds an implementation bridge from public-benefit eligibility to opt-in community-solar enrollment and a required minimum bill-credit discount. It does not establish completed enrollment, actual bill credits, net savings, energy-burden reduction, reliability, household security, persistence, or exit. The next test requires utility or program participant-level follow-up with bill timing and subscription cost preserved.
